project.title: VoRD: Vocabulary of Restrictive Datasets
project.description: Vocabulary for describing operational restrictions of SPARQL services, aligned with SPARQL Service Description and validated with SHACL and ShEx.

examples.label: Basic Service
examples.description: A minimal SPARQL service description with rate, result-size, and response-time restrictions.

examples.label: Exhaustive Service
examples.description: An example covering the core VoRD restriction classes and terms.

examples.label: Wikidata Rate Restrictions
examples.description: An example VoRD description for Wikidata's public SPARQL endpoint.

hierarchy.title: Ontology Structure
hierarchy.description: A curated overview of the main class and concept relationships in this ontology.

hero.headline: Operational restrictions for SPARQL services.
hero.body: VoRD lets SPARQL endpoint maintainers publish rate limits, quotas, result-size limits, timeouts, concurrency limits, and enforcement behavior in a machine-readable form.

resourcePanel.title: VoRD source artifacts
resourcePanel.body: Browse the authoritative vocabulary, validation shapes, ShEx schema, usage specification, and example service descriptions.

overviewCards.title: Vocabulary reference
overviewCards.body: Explore VoRD classes, properties, metrics, scopes, enforcement modes, and controlled concepts.

overviewCards.title: Interactive graph
overviewCards.body: Inspect the vocabulary structure with the local graph or the optional WebVOWL view.

overviewCards.title: Usage specification
overviewCards.body: Read the implementer-oriented profile for publishing restrictions on SPARQL services.

customSections.title: Validation and interoperability
customSections.body: VoRD descriptions extend SPARQL Service Description and can be checked with the supplied SHACL shapes or ShEx schema.
items: Use vord:hasRestriction to connect restrictions to an sd:Service.
Use vord:metric, vord:maxValue, vord:hasScope, and vord:enforcement for the core restriction pattern.
Use the examples as starting points for endpoint-specific service descriptions.
